title: Balanced localization and raw fraction comparison for finite coefficients
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and $E\subset L$ finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings $A_F=\mathcal O_F$ and chosen uniformizers $t_F$ for $F=E,L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. On its small pro-etale site put $B_{F,X}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A_F/t_F^n)_X$ and $F_X=B_{F,X}[1/t_F]$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Use sheaves of modules, sheaf tensor products and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal C_F(X)=D^b_c(X,A_F)$ for the completed integral category with compatible etale-origin witnesses, $Q_F:\mathcal C_F(X)\to\mathcal R_F(X)=\mathcal C_F(X)[1/t_F]$ for raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete, def-weil-pbc-rational-category], and $J_{F,X}(Q_FK)=F_X\otimes^L_{B_{F,X}}K$, $J_{F,X}(f/t_F^n)=t_F^{-n}(F_X\otimes^L f)$ [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]. Let $C_X=B_{L,X}\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}-$, with constructible restriction and raw rationalization $T_{L/E,X}$ [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

The integral coefficient map $i_X:B_{E,X}\to B_{L,X}$ is normalized by $\pi^L_n i_X=(\iota_n)_X\pi^E_n$, where $\iota_n:A_E/t_E^n\to A_L/t_L^n$ comes from inclusion. For every scheme map $g:X'\to X$ between schemes with the same hypotheses, the coefficient maps $c_{F,g}:g^{-1}B_{F,X}\to B_{F,X'}$ defined by finite projections [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] satisfy
$$i_{X'}c_{E,g}=c_{L,g}g^{-1}i_X.$$
Under continuous coefficient realization this square is precomposition by the geometric projection commuting with postcomposition by $E\hookrightarrow L$ [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations]. Its localization preserves the coefficient units; every nonzero constant of $E$ has inverse its constant reciprocal in $L_X$.

For $K\in\mathcal C_E(X)$ set $U_XK=L_X\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}K$. There are specified natural isomorphisms
$$s_K:L_X\otimes^L_{B_{L,X}}C_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}U_XK,\qquad t_K:L_X\otimes^L_{E_X}(E_X\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}U_XK.$$
They are the derived tensor composition comparisons: on every flat-term K-flat representative $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], scalar extension remains flat-term K-flat and both comparisons multiply the adjacent coefficient factors, $(l\otimes b)\otimes p\mapsto lb\otimes p$, with inverses inserting $1$. These formulas are independent of representatives and natural for all derived morphisms. The components $t_K^{-1}s_K$ define a natural isomorphism $\theta_{L/E,X}:J_{L,X}T_{L/E,X}\xrightarrow{\sim}(L_X\otimes^L_{E_X}-)J_{E,X}$ on raw rationalizations. Its naturality for $f/t_E^n$ is integral naturality multiplied by $t_E^{-n}$. More precisely, if $t_E^r(t_E^mf-t_E^nh)=0$, the images of $f/t_E^n$ and $h/t_E^m$ coincide after multiplying the resulting equality by $t_E^{-r-m-n}$; no torsion-free Hom hypothesis is imposed. Its inverse has components $s_K^{-1}t_K$.

For finite towers $E\subset L\subset M$ the successive $\theta$ comparisons agree with the direct comparison under the specified raw scalar associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. On the common K-flat models both flattened routes are $m\otimes l\otimes p\mapsto ml\otimes p$. For four nested fields the pentagon has flattened value $nml\otimes p$. For equality fields the literally identity raw scalar functor has the multiplication unitor comparison. These are equations of natural transformations on raw fractions as well as integral morphisms.

source.place: Tags 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition); Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 6.8.2 and Proposition 6.8.14; parent retained steps 1-4

proof.text: The restriction of $|\cdot|_L$ to $E$ is $|\cdot|_E$ by uniqueness of the extended absolute value. Thus inclusion carries $A_E$ into $A_L$ and $t_E$ into its maximal ideal. The DVR assertion gives $t_E=u t_L^e$ for a unit $u\in A_L$ and $e\geq1$. Consequently $t_E^nA_E$ maps into $t_L^nA_L$, so the maps $\iota_n$ exist and commute with quotient transitions. Their constant-sheaf maps and the projections of $B_{E,X}$ give a compatible family into $(A_L/t_L^n)_X$, hence the map $i_X$ with the required normalization. For the square with $g$, compose both routes with $\pi^L_n$. By the defining finite projections of $c_{F,g}$ they become the same map: inverse image of $\pi^E_n$, then the constant coefficient map induced by $\iota_n$, and the canonical inverse-image identification of constant sheaves. Naturality here just says that a locally constant section labelled $a$ is sent to the section labelled $\iota_n(a)$ on either route. The inverse-limit universal property now gives $i_{X'}c_{E,g}=c_{L,g}g^{-1}i_X$. In Lean, continuity is obtained by applying the already proved integralScalar_absoluteValue to the field algebra embedding and then using isometry continuity. The finite-projection characterization is pbcScalarCoefficientMap_exists; the geometric square follows from limit.hom_ext and naturality of the finite constant-coefficient maps.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59; finite-projection normalization, with the coefficient valuation facts explicitly cited

proof.text: Use the continuous-function identifications of the integral inverse limits and their sheaf localizations. Postcomposition by $A_E\hookrightarrow A_L$ has projections $(\iota_n)_X\pi^E_n$, so uniqueness into the inverse limit identifies it with $i_X$. The continuous coefficient realization intertwines coefficient postcomposition; geometric pullback is precomposition by the projection, which commutes with postcomposition by inclusion. Reduction modulo $t_F^n$ commutes with precomposition, so this geometric map has finite components $c_{g,n}g^{-1}\pi^F_n$. Uniqueness into the inverse limit therefore identifies it with the particular $c_{F,g}$ of Step 1. On constants both operations send $1$ to $1$. In $L_X$, the constant section with value $a\in E^\times$ has inverse the constant section with value $a^{-1}\in L$, since their pointwise products are $1$. In particular $t_E$ is invertible there. The induced localized map is explicitly $b/t_E^n\mapsto i_X(b)t_E^{-n}$ locally; it is well defined by the fraction relation, is unital, and agrees under continuous realization with postcomposition by $E\hookrightarrow L$. Thus the integral square localizes to the asserted unit-preserving square. For the geometric normalization, the finite_normalization fields identify each finiteIso with the canonical constant-sheaf comparison: sheafification uniqueness reduces this identification to constant sections. The integral_normalization fields then identify the completed projections with pointwise residue reduction. Naturality of the canonical constant comparison under pullback gives the finite squares, and the continuous residue cone limit gives their integral square. The localized coefficient square is obtained from the retained rationalBalancedIntegralNormalization statement and the two inclusion_normalization fields. Constant reciprocals use the sheafification adjunction and multiplicativity of the embedding; composition and the rational geometric square use pointwise postcomposition and continuousCoefficientPullback_naturality directly. S4 proves rationalBalancedIntegralNormalization by the normalized finite charts: the finite scalar square is checked after the canonical constant-sheaf comparison; the lifted quotient formula identifies the residue of the embedded integral value at each positive level. Injectivity of the ring equivalence to the compatible-family ring in lem-sfb-integers-profinite-tower then identifies the integral values, and applying Subtype.val gives the asserted field-value equation. The argument applies sectionwise for every point, including empty test objects vacuously and ramified coefficient embeddings.

Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ by the K-flat resolution theorem. Apply K-flat pullback preservation to the identity underlying topos with each of the coefficient maps $B_{E,X}\to B_{L,X}$, $B_{E,X}\to E_X$, $B_{L,X}\to L_X$, and $E_X\to L_X$. Each scalar extension of the relevant flat-term K-flat complex is again flat-term K-flat. Thus successive derived extensions can all be computed by successive ordinary sheaf tensors on these models. This invokes no flatness of a finite quotient coefficient map and imposes no boundedness on $P$.

source.place: Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat; resolution used in Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition

proof.text: Apply the canonical successive-derived-scalar comparison first to $B_{E,X}\to B_{L,X}\to L_X$ and then to $B_{E,X}\to E_X\to L_X$. These are the specified $s_K$ and $t_K$, with common target $U_XK$. With coefficient factors written on the left, their maps are $(l\otimes b)\otimes p\mapsto lb\otimes p$ and $(l\otimes e)\otimes p\mapsto le\otimes p$; the inverses send $l\otimes p$ to $(l\otimes1)\otimes p$. The coefficient factors have degree zero, so this convention introduces no sign. The formulas respect the balancing relations and commute with the differential, and the composites are the identity by balancing against $1$. Importantly, the cited comparison is already natural on the entire derived category, not only for chain maps between chosen models. Its canonical K-flat computation, together with the change-of-rings independence of resolutions, identifies these displayed chain maps with that comparison for every $P$. Hence the formulas are independent of representatives and natural for all derived morphisms. The arbitrary-derived-morphism naturality clause is proved directly by identifying pbcReductionNormalization.hom with the component of Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso and applying naturality of that natural transformation.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat, specialized to coefficient maps

proof.text: On $\mathcal C_E(X)$ form $\eta_K=t_K^{-1}s_K$, with inverse $s_K^{-1}t_K$. The actual integral scalar functor restricts and rationalizes to $T_{L/E,X}$, while $J_{F,X}$ has exactly the displayed scalar-localization and fraction formulas. Therefore the two integral functors connected by $\eta$ are the restrictions of $J_{L,X}T_{L/E,X}$ and $(L_X\otimes^L_{E_X}-)J_{E,X}$. They are semilinear from $A_E$ to $L$: a coefficient scalar moves across the balancing relation, and degree-zero scalar multiplication commutes with the derived comparisons. By Step 2 the image of $t_E$ is a unit in $L$. Apply semilinear scalar localization with target $D(L_X)$, viewed as an $L$-linear category and localized at $1$. It extends $\eta$ and its inverse uniquely to the raw rational category. This gives $\theta$ with the stated components, and its naturality equation at $f/t_E^n$ is the integral naturality equation multiplied by $t_E^{-n}$. No change of objects or idempotent completion is involved. Given the retained component naturality statement, NatIso.ofComponents constructs theta. The stated existence and uniqueness follows by equality of the hom components, using extensionality of isomorphisms and natural transformations.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), pp. 61-62; agent expansion of the balanced comparison on raw fractions

proof.text: Work in the raw localized Hom module itself, before applying either realization functor. Let c be the image of t and v its specified localization reciprocal. Apply the R-linear localization map to t^r(t^m f-t^n h)=0. The unit c^r can be cancelled in this localized module, yielding c^m Q(f)=c^n Q(h). Multiply the desired equation v^n Q(f)=v^m Q(h) by the unit c^(m+n); using c^a v^a=1 reduces it to that cross equation. Apply the map function of each of the two functors to this single equality. No faithfulness, semilinearity or torsion-free property of the integral Hom module is used.

source.place: Tag 00CO, definition-localization; explicit equality-of-fractions computation for module Hom groups

proof.text: For $E\subset L\subset M$, compute the diagram on a flat-term K-flat $B_{E,X}$-model. The integral coefficient associators identify successive scalar extension with direct scalar extension by the normalized multiplication comparison. The successive-derived-scalar comparison is natural in the coefficient maps and its iterated comparisons agree. Flattening to $M_X\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}K$, both routes therefore send $m\otimes l\otimes p$ to $ml\otimes p$ (any intervening integral coefficient factor is multiplied into the same product). Since these are equal chain maps under the canonical computation comparisons, they give equal derived natural transformations. The specified raw associators are the rationalizations of these balanced comparisons, so the semilinear localization theorem preserves this equation, including whiskering: the same square commutes on every raw fraction. For the normalized tower, a general category-theoretic conjugation calculation transports the raw tower equation along the three specified pbcStageNormalization isomorphisms. The proof uses naturality of the inverse middle normalization and of the raw theta, with cancellation of inverse components.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition, iterated coefficient-map specialization; raw associators as specified in prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension

proof.text: With four nested fields, flatten every parenthesization to the final coefficient sheaf tensored with the original $P$. The five routes around the pentagon all multiply the three degree-zero coefficient entries and send $n\otimes m\otimes l\otimes p$ to $nml\otimes p$; associativity of ring multiplication gives their equality. The iterated-comparison clause identifies these chain maps with the canonical derived comparisons. For an equality extension, the chosen raw functor is literally the identity; use the multiplication unitor to identify $B_{E,X}\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}K$ with $K$. Then $t_K^{-1}s_K$ is the comparison to $E_X\otimes^L_{E_X}J_EK$, with inverse multiplication, and the unit diagrams reduce to $1x=x=x1$. Localization preserves these identity, composite and whiskered equations, so the pentagon and unit equations hold as natural-transformation equations on the raw rational categories as well. For the normalized identity, keep the ordinary and derived multiplication witnesses from rationalBalancedIdentity. At equal fields pbcStageNormalization is the raw tensor unit followed by the equality-to-identity transport. Functoriality and the inverse-component equations cancel the raw unit, giving exactly the required equality transport. S4 proves rationalBalancedPentagon by the existing norm_assoc helper in CompletedPullbackReductionCoherence: it is the associativity equation of the unit-normalized derived scalar comparisons. The raw scalar associators are tensor-with-one images of these integral comparisons. The pure-tensor formula for scalar extension and ScalarLocalization.composition_tmul lift the integral equation to raw morphisms. Applying the realization functor and postcomposing with the common theta component gives the asserted equation. Associativity of composition of the coefficient algebra embeddings identifies the two direct target functors. No representative, unit normalization, or fraction naturality assumption is added.
